newsitem.title: USA: U.S. December S&P 500 ends quiet afternoon higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. December S&P 500 ends quiet afternoon higher.

text.p: U.S. December Standard and Poor's 500 futures rallied early to post a new contract and all-time high, then meandered in slightly positive territory for the rest of the day.
Trading was quiet all afternoon, traders said.

On the heels of a rally to all-time highs last week, December posted another high early Monday at 709.90 as good buying materialized from several firms. The early rally triggered buy stops at 707.50 and 707.80, but strong buying soon dwindled and the market drifted.
A late afternoon foray to session lows at 706.50 was tied to Treasury bond futures weakness. Once that market closed, December S&Ps drifted to midrange again, traders said.
Support for early this week at 706.10 and 704.40 held, traders said. Resistance stands at 710.00, 711.25 and 713.00.
Traders said many players appeared to be on the sidelines ahead of corporate earnings this week and U.S. economic data.

One S&P trader said some players appeared skeptical that Motorola's third quarter 1996 earnings would be under pressure, as some analysts had forecast. Motorola earnings were due today after the market close.

In view of last week's run higher in S&Ps, some traders said they expected profit-taking to set in later this week. December surged more than 20 points from last Monday's session low at 689.20 to today's high at 709.90, a distance some traders said was too far too fast. They said a corrective pullback was due.
Others said the bullish tempo was intact, and saw 710.00 and 713.00 as targets this week.
The first piece of the U.S. inflation picture will be released on Friday. September producer prices were forecast up 0.3 percent overall and 0.2 percent excluding food and energy.

KBT Value Lines finished down 1.20 points at 652.30, New Composites settled up 0.10 points to 377.40, Nikkei 225 lost 90.0 to 21,150, Midcap 400s were down 0.50 at 247.70, and Nasdaq 100s were 6.70 points higher at 773.95. Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuter.com
